summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and hypogammaglobulinemia was admitted for monitored IVIG infusion due to prior intolerance of new treatments. He reported mild dehydration and recent diarrhea but was otherwise in his usual state of health. On hospital day one, he received 30 grams of IVIG with only mild hypertension. On day two, he developed transient chest pressure and shortness of breath associated with elevated blood pressure, which resolved with sublingual nitroglycerin and antihypertensive effect. Serial cardiac enzymes were negative and EKG unchanged, ruling out acute myocardial infarction. He also experienced nausea, resolved with antiemetics. He received 4 liters of IV normal saline for hydration support. By hospital day three, he was asymptomatic and requested discharge. No medication changes were made. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue baseline therapies and maintain hydration.
